PACKET-10: UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

EXPOSURE STATEMENT
- Nothing in my context proposed an identification of the work or author before or during this reading. I used no edition or catalogue and did no search.
- The images themselves show modern pencil shelf labels: "Stams, STA, Frg. 85-1r", "85-2r", "85-1v" and "85-2v". They also show pencil "4° Ms 12" and what may be a date ("c. 1280"?) on the 2r strip, plus large pencil numerals in the right margin of 1r (".. 7 / 3 / ... 1320"?). I report these as visible features. I did not use them to interpret the text.
- What I did beyond reading PROMPT.md and the images: I ran `ls` on the packet directory to get the image filenames. That showed a packet.json, which I did not open. I also created /tmp/stams4-read/responses/ to hold this file. No other directory was opened.
- All 23 images loaded and none failed.

CONVENTIONS
- Expansions are in ( ). A reading followed by (?) is uncertain. [illegible] marks text I cannot read; [hole] marks physical loss. Line numbers ("Lnn") are counted from the top of the named image, and a line cut by the image edge counts as line 1. In the badly damaged verso areas the counts are approximate. Where crops overlap, I transcribe each line once and note the overlap.
- These are draft readings. Many abbreviation expansions (especially q(uonia)m, q(uo)d and (con)- forms) are tentative.

======================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observations only)
======================================================================
- image-001 is an overview of face 1. It shows two horizontal parchment strips. The upper strip is labelled "Frg. 85-2r" and the lower one "Frg. 85-1r". Each strip carries text from two columns per page, and a fold or gutter runs vertically near the middle. The strips seem to come from a bifolium or from two adjacent leaves (a tentative interpretation): each strip shows the lower part of 2 columns + 2 columns. Ruled lines are visible. The script is a small gothic textualis/notula-type book hand with heavy abbreviation, and the ink is brown.
- image-011 is an overview of face 2. It shows the same two strips reversed ("85-2v" upper, "85-1v" lower). The surface is heavily abraded and covered with brown residue in broad brush-like streaks (paste or glue?). Text is legible mainly in clean bands along the top and bottom edges. Blue ink is visible: paragraph marks or initials in image-013, image-014, image-021 and the overview.
- Text features seen on face 1:
  * Lemma openings are often underlined, introduced by "¶ De(inde) cum d(icit)" and followed by a paraph ("¶"). Examples: image-002 L10 "v(er)u(m) aut(em) ... t(ri)angl(u)s"; image-004 L13 "Circulo(?) aut(em) ... i(m)po(ssibi)le". New sections start with an indented underlined lemma ending "et c(etera)", e.g. image-002 L23 "¶ Igit(ur) est demo(n)st(ratio)(?) et c(etera)", image-004 L29 "¶ Circulo(?) aut(em) q(uonia)m i(m)po(ssibi)le et c(etera)", image-007 L14 "¶ Oportet aut(em) non late(re) et c(etera)".
  * Tentative interpretation: this is continuous commentary prose that quotes short lemmata from a base text. I can see no separate base-text column.
  * Marginalia: a cursive marginal word near image-003 col b L22 ("Scie"/"Sciē"?), marks such as "R(?)", "p(?)o" and a pointing sign beside image-003 col c, and "Secundo"(?) in the margin by image-006 col c L7 (cursive; reading uncertain). There are small marginal letters beside image-004 col c L7 and L16, and a few interlinear corrections or additions, e.g. "dici" above the line in image-008 col b L8.
  * Deletion: image-004 col c L4 has words struck through ("sunt non n(?) p(?)t") after "si p(ri)n(cipi)a".
- Unread or only partly read: the lower half of face-1 lower-strip col a (cropped at the left edge, line starts lost); the narrow right column on the upper strip (only line starts visible); most of face 2 below the clean top band.
- Recommendations: a raking-light or UV image of face 2, and a wider crop of the left edge of 85-1r (col a), would help.
